Step 1: Clean the Slate and Get the Tools
First, make sure your environment is activated. Then, we will install all the necessary build tools and dependencies directly from conda-forge so they all share the exact same C++ standard.

Bash
conda activate omega

# Install the modern C++ toolchain and required dependencies (zlib, bzip2, pcre2)
conda install -c conda-forge cmake make pkg-config "gcc_linux-64>=13" "gxx_linux-64>=13" zlib bzip2 pcre2
Step 2: Build the Core Library (libcifpp)
DSSP cannot be built until its parser library, libcifpp, is built and installed first.

Run these commands one by one to download, configure, and install it. Notice the special RPATH flags in the CMake command—this is the magic that prevents the Segmentation Faults.

Bash
# Go to your working directory (e.g., ~/omega)
cd ~/omega

# Download the source code
git clone https://github.com/PDB-REDO/libcifpp.git
cd libcifpp

# Configure with RPATH pointing exclusively to your Conda environment
cmake -S . -B build \
  -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=$CONDA_PREFIX \
  -DCMAKE_INSTALL_RPATH=$CONDA_PREFIX/lib \
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_WITH_INSTALL_RPATH=ON

# Compile and install (this will take a few minutes)
cmake --build build -j 4
cmake --install build
(Note: During the install step, it should automatically download mmcif_pdbx.dic and components.cif safely into your Conda prefix).

Step 3: Build dssp
Now that the parser is installed, we move back out and build the actual dssp application.

Bash
cd ~/omega

# Download the DSSP source code
git clone https://github.com/PDB-REDO/dssp.git
cd dssp

# Configure with the same RPATH magic
cmake -S . -B build \
  -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=$CONDA_PREFIX \
  -DCMAKE_INSTALL_RPATH=$CONDA_PREFIX/lib \
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_WITH_INSTALL_RPATH=ON

# Compile and install
cmake --build build -j 4
cmake --install build
Step 4: Verify the Installation
Before touching Python, let's verify that the RPATH fix worked and the binary is stable.

First, check that it correctly bound to your Conda libraries, not your system libraries:

Bash
ldd $CONDA_PREFIX/bin/mkdssp | grep libstdc++
(This should output a path containing anaconda3/envs/omega/lib/, proving it is isolated).

Finally, test the executable on your file:

Bash
mkdssp cif_files/5JYT.cif
